Definition: from G2314; to resist deity:--fight against God.
BiblicalUsage: theomachéō stands behind the English phrase to fight against God. In Acts 5:39, if it be of God. The King James Version reads the word here, while the Greek text behind the modern editions reads differently: SBL reads θεομάχοι, lemma θεομάχος (G2314).
TheologicalSignificance: I believe I will not fight against God, and I take Gamaliel’s warning as my own.
